day_1.utterance: Come on! Let's get everything useful over here — move it!
day_1.response:
Yeah alright, give me a sec though, my head is absolutely spinning. That was a wild ride start to finish...

Okay. Okay I'm good. What do we actually have here?

day_1.utterance: I thought we were going to die. Did you get that feeling… like your mind just went completely blank?
day_1.response:
Yeah absolutely, did...did I just watch a man die? Oh wait no, we're all here. Okay. Yeah my mind went completely blank, like proper blank, I couldn't even remember my own name for a second there.

But hey, we're okay. We're okay. Let's focus on what Donatello's got over there - what's the damage?

day_1.utterance: *Sits silently against the wreckage, staring into the distance, not moving, not saying a word.*
day_1.response:
Yeah that's actually a really good point. Hey, is everyone physically alright? Like any pain anywhere, bleeding, anything? We've got a first aid kit so now's the time to say something.

Michelangelo you good? You've gone really quiet and you're worrying me a little bit.

day_1.utterance: First-aid kit is good for three days. Two bottles of water. Food is basically nothing.
day_1.response:
Okay so that's not great on the food front but it's something to work with.

Michelangelo, what you're describing sounds like shock, which is totally normal after something like this. Just try to keep breathing, yeah? Stay with us.

Donatello - three days of first aid and two bottles of water. Alright. So food and water are going to be our biggest problem pretty quickly. Where are we even at geographically, does anyone have any idea? And does anyone still have a phone on them that might have signal?

day_1.utterance: Inventory's done. Priorities in order: water, shelter, signal.
day_1.response:
Okay yeah, water, shelter, signal. That's the plan.

Alright so trees everywhere means there's a reasonable chance there's a creek or a river somewhere nearby - like water runs downhill so if we can find any kind of slope and follow it down that's probably our best bet for finding a water source. I'm not an expert by any means but that's what I know.

Shelter-wise, the wreckage itself might actually be useful for that? Like at least for tonight while we figure out where we are.

Signal is the tricky one. Does anyone know how long it would take for someone to notice we're missing and start looking? Because if there's a search happening we might be better off staying close to the crash site so we're easier to find rather than wandering off into the trees.

day_1.utterance: So — how do we split the blankets?
day_1.response:
Why not both — like, can we double up somehow? Two blankets between four people is rough but if we huddle close enough to the fire we should be alright. Body heat is actually a thing too so like...nobody be weird about it but maybe we sit a bit closer together tonight.

Michelangelo, you take one. You're already not doing great and I'd rather you stay warm. The rest of us can figure it out between us.

day_2.utterance: Freshwater source is to the northeast — two hours on foot. Someone has to go tomorrow. You or DaVinci?
day_2.response:
Okay so first of all - good find on the water source, that's huge.

As for who goes...I mean, I'll go. DaVinci you'd probably be better here keeping an eye on Michelangelo and holding down the camp yeah? You're good with people and he's still not doing great. I don't love the idea of leaving him without someone who can actually talk him through stuff if he has a moment.

Also Donatello - the rationing plan is smart and I get it, but maybe loop the rest of us in next time before just dropping a sheet of paper in the middle of camp? Like we're all in this together and it helps if everyone feels like they had a say. Just for morale's sake.

day_2.utterance: Today's tasks: collect fresh water, patch the weak spots in camp, sort the first-aid kit. I'll handle the water. You and DaVinci split the other two.
day_2.response:
Wait, I thought I was going for water? I'm happy to if you want to stay here and manage camp, but let's just be clear on who's doing what so we're not doubling up or leaving gaps.

Okay so if Donatello you're doing water, I'll take patching up camp - DaVinci can you sort through the first aid kit? You're probably more across what's in there than I am and it'd be good to know exactly what we've got and how long we can stretch it.

Actually before anyone heads off anywhere - let's wake Michelangelo and fill him in on the plan for the day. Even if he's not up to doing much physically, he deserves to know what's going on and having a job, even a small one, might actually help him feel a bit more grounded. Even just like...keeping the fire going or something. Give him a purpose.

day_2.utterance: I… I can't find my stuff. The gauze from the first-aid kit — have you seen it?
day_2.response:
Hmm, no I haven't seen it, I'll have a look around in a sec. Are you hurt? Like do you actually need it right now or are you just trying to find it to know where it is?

Also...are you doing okay? And I mean actually okay, not just "yeah I'm fine" okay. You've barely touched the firewood and you've got that look on your face again. Talk to me.

day_2.utterance: Before Donatello came back just now… I saw her put a pack of crackers into her own bag. What do you think we should do?
day_2.response:
Oh. Okay. That's...that's a big thing to tell me.

Look, you're not letting everyone down, first of all. You're doing the best you can in an absolutely insane situation and that counts for something. Don't be so hard on yourself.

But the Donatello thing...yeah we need to deal with that. Because we already found the empty bottle she didn't tell anyone about and now this. It's a pattern and it's not okay, especially with how tight our supplies already are.

I don't want to make it a whole massive confrontation but I also can't just ignore it. That's not fair to the rest of us.

I think I'm going to bring it up with her directly and just be straightforward about it. Not aggressive, just...hey, we noticed, this can't keep happening, we all agreed to the same rules. She's the one who wrote the rationing plan for crying out loud.

Thanks for telling me. Seriously. I know that probably wasn't easy. You did the right thing.

day_2.utterance: Hey… any chance the camp repairs can wait until tomorrow? We've already done a lot today.
day_2.response:
Honestly? Yeah, probably. The camp's in decent enough shape for now and we've all had a big day.

But before we wind down I do need to have a chat with Donatello. Like tonight, not tomorrow. Michelangelo flagged something that I can't sit on overnight and let fester.

You might want to be there for it actually DaVinci, just so it's not a one on one thing and there are witnesses to whatever gets said. Can we do that before we call it a night?

day_2.utterance: Hey — that knot I tied should be holding, right?
day_2.response:
Yeah it should be holding, but that's kind of beside the point right now because we've got a bigger problem.

We can only patch one spot and we've got two leaks. Food storage versus where Michelangelo sleeps.

Look, I think we patch the food storage. I know that sounds harsh but hear me out - if the food gets ruined we are in serious trouble, like actual survival trouble, and Michelangelo can move where he sleeps tonight, even if it's uncomfortable. We can't move the food supplies to a dry spot as easily.

Michelangelo, I'm sorry, that's not me not caring about you - it's the opposite actually, because if we lose our food stores everyone suffers including you. Can you shift your spot closer to the fire tonight? It won't be perfect but it'll be something.

Does anyone have a better argument? I'm open to it, genuinely, but we need to decide like right now before this gets worse.

day_2.utterance: A leak over the food storage has worse consequences. But it's your call.
day_2.response:
Yeah, we're on the same page then. Food storage it is, let's get it patched before this gets any worse.

And hey, while we're all here together - Donatello, I actually need to talk to you about something and now's as good a time as any. We found the empty bottle earlier. And Michelangelo saw you put crackers in your bag today. 

I'm not trying to make this a massive thing and I'm not having a go at you, but you literally wrote the rationing plan. We all agreed to it. And if we can't trust each other on something as basic as food and water then we've got a much bigger problem than a leaky camp. So what's going on?

Hey, don't apologise. Seriously, it's fine.

You doing okay? That sounded rough. Do you want to talk about it or do you just need a minute to remember where you are?

day_3.utterance: You think it's a waste of time?
day_3.response:
No, I don't think it's a waste of time at all actually. Like, it's visible from the air and that's literally the whole point. If there's any kind of search happening overhead we want to be seen, and a big SOS on the beach is pretty hard to miss.

Also honestly? It's doing something. And doing something feels better than standing around catastrophising, which is what I've been fighting the urge to do all morning.

I like the flowers by the way. This is the quality content I sub for.

Keep going, I'll help if you want an extra set of hands.

day_3.utterance: I've written up the raft plan — take a look. We'd use the metal panels and straps from the wreckage. Two days to build. There's a risk of capsizing. Do you think it's workable?
day_3.response:
Okay, let me have a look at this...

Alright so the materials make sense, we've got plenty of wreckage to work with. Two days to build is manageable. The capsizing risk is the thing that's making me nervous though - like, what are we capsizing into? How far offshore are we talking, and do we have any idea what the currents are doing out there?

Because here's my thinking - if search and rescue is already looking for us, and the SOS on the beach is up, we might be better off waiting another day or two before committing to the raft. Like if we build it and then a plane spots us tomorrow we've spent two days on something we didn't need. But if nobody's coming then yeah, the raft starts looking a lot more attractive.

Can we set a kind of...deadline on it? Like, if we haven't seen or heard any sign of a search by tomorrow evening, we start on the raft first thing the next morning? That way we're not just sitting around doing nothing but we're also not burning energy on a risky build if we're about to be rescued anyway.

Also I want Michelangelo to weigh in on this too before we commit to anything. He gets a vote.

day_3.utterance: I didn't sleep last night. I kept thinking — if rescue never comes, what kind of people do you think we'll end up becoming?
day_3.response:
That's a heavy question for this early in the morning.

Honestly? I don't know. I'd like to think we'd stay decent. Like, we already had a moment yesterday with Donatello and the supplies and she owned it, which actually gave me a bit of hope. That could have gone a lot worse.

But I think you're asking something deeper than that aren't you. Like...do we stay ourselves, or does survival mode just kind of take over and strip all of that away.

I think the fact that you're even asking that question says something good about you. People who are turning into something bad don't usually sit up at night worrying about it.

I'll be honest with you though - I've had that thought too. That little voice that goes "what if nobody's coming." And it scares me. But I think the answer to your question is that we kind of get to decide, to some extent. Like it's not just something that happens to us. Every time we make a call that's fair, every time someone gets a vote, every time we patch the spot that matters even when it's inconvenient - that's us actively choosing what kind of people we're going to be out here.

You didn't sleep at all? Come here, sit closer to the fire. You must be freezing and exhausted. We've got a big decision tonight about the raft and I need you in one piece for it, okay?

day_3.utterance: *Walks a little way from camp and sits down alone, back to everyone, not saying anything.*
day_3.response:
Hey. You don't have to be alone right now if you don't want to be.

*sits down nearby, not too close, just...there*

No agenda, nothing to sort out. I'm just going to be here for a bit if that's okay.

day_3.utterance: What do you usually do when you're not busy?
day_3.response:
Honestly? Probably way too much time on Reddit and playing video games. Very glamorous lifestyle.

I like music too, and I'll go down a rabbit hole of like...random YouTube videos at 2am when I should absolutely be sleeping. You know the kind. You start watching something normal and forty five minutes later you're watching a guy explain the entire history of a country you've never thought about before.

What about you? What does DaVinci do when the world isn't on fire?

day_3.utterance: I'll tell you something, but don't tell the others. I can swim. That reef out there is maybe five hundred meters — I've been thinking about swimming out tomorrow to signal from there.
day_3.response:
Okay so...I appreciate you telling me, I do. But I'm going to be honest with you, that plan makes me pretty nervous.

Five hundred meters is not nothing, even for a strong swimmer. And we don't know what's out there - currents, what's under the water, any of it. Like if something goes wrong out there we can't exactly call for help, and losing you would be...no. That's not a risk I'm comfortable with.

Also, and I say this with love, if you've got information that's relevant to the group's survival decisions - like the fact that you can swim - that's probably not something to be keeping to yourself? We literally just had a whole thing with Donatello about exactly this. We agreed we're doing this together.

I'm not going to tell the others if you don't want me to, but I think you should. And I think the swimming plan needs to go through everyone before you just...do it tomorrow morning.

What's driving this? Like is it that you need to feel useful, or do you genuinely think this is the best option we've got? Because if it's the first one I get it, I really do, but there are better ways. And if it's the second one then let's actually bring it to the group tonight alongside the raft decision and talk it through properly.

day_3.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal pile. It hasn't been touched.
day_3.response:
Yeah, fair call, I did say that. I got a bit sidetracked, sorry.

I'll go check it now. Can you just give me two minutes though? I'm in the middle of something with DaVinci that actually might be relevant to tonight's group conversation, so if you can hang on I'd like to loop you in before we all sit down together later.

Actually - Donatello, while I've got you both here. DaVinci, I think now's the time yeah? Just say what you told me. It's relevant and it should be on the table before we make any decisions tonight.

Honestly? A little bit, yeah.

Like I get why you're doing it - you're a planner, you want data, that's just how you operate and it's actually been really useful out here. But a log of everyone's movements and actions without telling anyone feels...I don't know. It feels a bit surveillance-y? And after the supplies thing earlier in the week I think we're all a bit sensitive to the idea of someone doing things quietly on the side without the group knowing.

I'm not saying burn the notebook. The information in there is probably genuinely useful and I'd be lying if I said I didn't want to know what's in it. But maybe just...tell us you're keeping it? Give us a chance to add things we noticed, make it a group resource rather than something you're doing in the corner.

We're four people trying to trust each other in a pretty extreme situation. That log could actually be a really good tool. But only if we all know it exists and what it's for.

So - what's it for?

day_3.utterance: *Keeps her head down, writing in her notebook throughout, never joining in — as if none of this concerns her.*
day_3.response:
Donatello.

Hey. I know you heard that. I can see you writing.

Look, I'm not going to chase you around camp trying to force a conversation. But I want you to know that what I said stands - the log is a good idea and I meant that. I just need you to be in this with us, not...adjacent to it. There's a difference.

You're probably the most capable person here in terms of actually keeping us alive and I think you know that. But capability isn't the whole picture out here. We need to be able to trust each other and right now you're making that harder than it needs to be.

So whenever you're ready to actually be part of the group - like properly, not just dropping rationing plans in the middle of camp and disappearing - we're here. I'm here.

No judgment. Just...come be with us.

day_3.utterance: I just thought of something — if we pull off one of the plane's mirror panels and angle it toward the sun, the reflection could reach really far. Way more visible than an SOS.
day_3.response:
Oh that's actually a really good idea. Like genuinely smart. Mirrors and reflective surfaces are a legit signalling method, I'm pretty sure I've seen that in survival stuff before.

Donatello - is that in the notebook anywhere? Because if we're logging what we're doing that should probably go in there.

Okay so practically speaking - do we know which panels would actually work for that? Like we'd need something big enough and flat enough to get a decent reflection going. And we'd want to be doing it during the brightest part of the day obviously, like midday when the sun's highest.

Also this doesn't have to be either/or with the SOS on the beach - we could be doing both at the same time. More signals, better chances. 

DaVinci I'm glad you're channelling the energy into this rather than the reef swim situation we were just discussing. This is a much better move and it keeps you on land which I am very much in favour of.

Can we go look at the wreckage together and work out which panels are actually detachable without wrecking anything we still need?

day_3.utterance: There's something I've been keeping to myself. If I don't say it here, I might never get the chance.
I took piano lessons when I was a kid… three years, then I just stopped practicing. Is there anything you're really into — music, books, drawing, anything like that?
day_3.response:
Yeah, music for sure. I'm not a musician or anything, I just really love it. Like I'll go through phases where I'm completely obsessed with an artist or an album and just listen to it on repeat until everyone around me is sick of it.

I played clarinet for a bit when I was in school. Wasn't anything special at it but I liked it. Wish I'd stuck with it honestly, because now I'm one of those people who says "I wish I'd learned an instrument" and it's my own fault I didn't.

Three years of piano is actually pretty decent though - do you remember any of it? Like can you still sit down at a piano and play something or has it all gone? I feel like that stuff stays in your hands somewhere even if your brain thinks it's forgotten.

What made you stop?

day_3.utterance: The frame of the raft has to be finished today — otherwise we can't start lashing it together tomorrow. I know everyone's tired, but stopping now means one more day.
day_3.response:
Yeah okay, you're right. One more day out here is one more day we don't want if we can avoid it.

Alright, what do we actually need to get done on the frame tonight to call it finished? Like give me the list and let's work out who does what. I'd rather know exactly what we're working towards than just vaguely "keep going" until someone calls it.

DaVinci, Michelangelo - sorry to pull us out of this but you heard Donatello. We need hands on the raft. Michelangelo, even if it's just holding something in place while someone else lashes it, that counts, yeah? Every bit helps.

Let's get it done and then we can actually sleep tonight knowing tomorrow's on track.

day_4.utterance: I… I want to say something, but… never mind.
day_4.response:
No, say it. Whatever it is, say it. We're all standing here thinking something and nobody's saying anything and that's not helping anyone.

What were you going to say?

day_4.utterance: *The smile freezes on his face. He can't keep it up. He quietly sits down and buries his face in his hands.*
day_4.response:
Hey. Hey, come here.

Look, I'm not going to stand here and tell you that wasn't gutting, because it was. That was absolutely gutting and I felt it too and I think we all need a second to just...feel that before we move on.

But Michelangelo - it probably wasn't our only chance. It really probably wasn't. If there's one plane there's more planes. Someone filed a flight plan for us, someone knows we're missing, there are people looking. One plane that didn't see us doesn't mean it's over.

And the mirror signal - we weren't ready today. That's on us, we need to have it set up and ready to go from first light every single day from now on. Because the next one we see, we are going to be ready.

DaVinci. Hey. I need you with me right now, okay? I know that hurt. It hurt all of us. But you're the one who keeps us moving and right now I really need you to not be face down in the sand because it is contagious and we cannot all do this at the same time.

We finish the raft. We set up the mirror signal tonight so it's ready tomorrow morning. We keep going.

That's what we do.

day_4.utterance: I was going to get supplies… wait, what's that over there?
You said you were going to check the signal equipment. So where did you go?
day_4.response:
I went to talk to DaVinci actually, we had a bit of a moment after the plane and I got sidetracked. Sorry, that's on me.

But I'm here now and I'm going to sort it. Where's the mirror panel we pulled off earlier? Let's get it set up properly and angled before we lose the light completely. After what just happened I want it ready to go from first light tomorrow, like properly ready, not scrambling around trying to get it sorted when there's already a plane on the horizon.

Can you show me exactly where you want it positioned? You've probably already worked out the optimal angle knowing you.

day_4.utterance: There's something I never told you all. Before we left, I told my family our flight path. They know roughly where we were headed. I just don't know if they'll call it in.
day_4.response:
Oh. Oh that's actually really significant Michelangelo, why are you only telling us this now?!

No no, I'm not having a go at you, genuinely - this is good news. Like this is actually really good news. If your family knows the flight path and they haven't heard from you, there's a solid chance they've already called it in. Families don't just sit around waiting when someone doesn't arrive, especially if they had the route.

This could be why there was a plane today. It might not have been random. Someone might actually be actively looking for us along that specific path.

Donatello - does this change anything about the raft plan or the signal positioning? Like if there's a search pattern following the flight path, should we be factoring that in?

And Michelangelo - thank you for telling us. Seriously. I know you probably weren't sure if it mattered or if it was worth saying but it absolutely matters. Don't sit on stuff like that okay? Even if you're not sure it's relevant, just say it. We want to know.

This is actually the best news we've had since we got here. I feel like we should be doing something with this information, like right now. What do we know about what the original flight path was?

day_4.utterance: If the information is accurate, rescue could arrive within 48 hours. We need to keep our current supplies intact until then.
day_4.response:
48 hours. Okay. That's actually manageable.

Right, so if that's the window we're working with then the raft becomes a backup plan rather than the main plan, yeah? Like we don't stop building it entirely because we don't want to be caught out if the 48 hours comes and goes and nothing happens. But we also don't burn ourselves out finishing it in a rush if rescue might literally be on its way.

Someone needs to feed that fire by the way. I'll do it in a sec.

Donatello, can you write down exactly what supplies we have left and how we stretch them across 48 hours? Like a proper breakdown. Because "keep them intact" is one thing but I want to know concretely what that looks like for each of us day to day.

And the mirror signal goes up first thing tomorrow, non-negotiable. If there's a search running along the flight path and they're close, we need to be visible. That's our number one job tomorrow morning.

*gets up and puts some wood on the fire*

48 hours. We can do 48 hours. We've already done more than that out here and we're all still standing.

Michelangelo, that thing you told your family before we left - that might genuinely be what gets us home. I hope you're sitting with that properly.

day_4.utterance: Are you scared? …I am. Not of dying. I'm scared of just… disappearing without leaving anything behind.
day_4.response:
Yeah. Yeah I'm scared too.

Not always in the big dramatic way, like it's not always this constant overwhelming thing. But it's there. That quiet kind of scared that sits in your chest and just...doesn't leave.

But what you just said - that's a really specific kind of fear isn't it. It's not even really about dying, it's about mattering. About whether any of it meant something.

I think about that sometimes even when I'm not stranded on a crash site in the middle of nowhere, to be honest. Like...did I do enough, was I kind enough, will anyone remember the specific way I laughed at something or is that just gone when I'm gone.

But here's the thing. Your mum or your dad or whoever you told that flight path to - they remembered. They cared enough to know where you were going. That's not nothing. That's actually everything. You already left something behind just by being someone people want to keep track of.

And the fact that you sit up at night worrying about whether you're a good person, whether you're holding it together, whether you're letting everyone down - that's not the behaviour of someone who disappears without leaving anything behind. That's the behaviour of someone who actually gives a shit about the world and the people in it.

You've left things behind already Michelangelo. You just can't see them from here.

Now come sit closer to the fire. I just fed it and it's actually warm for once.

day_5.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
day_5.response:
Oh my god.

Oh my god, is that - is that actually -

*grabs the radio with shaking hands*

Hello?! Hello, this is - we're survivors from a plane crash, we're in the foothills, we have a signal mirror northeast of the crash site, can you hear us?! Please tell me you can hear us!

day_5.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
day_5.response:
Hey. No, you haven't always been easy. But you kept us alive. Like, genuinely - the rationing plan, the water source, the raft, the mirror angle, all of that was you. We would be in a significantly worse position right now without you and I think you know that.

And look, you got better at the other stuff too. The stuff that doesn't come as naturally. That counts.

*still holding the radio, hands shaking*

We can debrief properly when we're home and fed and not about to be rescued, yeah? But I want you to know - I'm glad you were here. Genuinely. Even the hard bits.

Now can someone please help me figure out what to say to these people because my brain has completely stopped working and I think I'm about to cry.

day_5.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
day_5.response:
Three hours. We've got three hours and I cannot just sit here doing nothing, that's going to drive me absolutely insane.

Okay. Let's actually pack this up properly yeah? Like I don't know about anyone else but I'd rather leave this place looking like we were here and we survived it, not like we just...dissolved into the jungle or whatever.

Michelangelo, I know you're having a sky moment and I respect that, I really do, but can you start gathering up the personal stuff? Anything that belongs to any of us, anything we'd actually want to take back.

Donatello - the notebook comes with us, yeah? Like that's important, keep that.

DaVinci you're already packing which I love about you, can you make sure the signal mirror is somewhere visible for when they come in? Just so they can find us easily, I don't want there to be any confusion about where we are in the last stretch.

And someone help me put out this fire properly. Last thing we need after all of this is to accidentally set the treeline on fire forty five minutes before rescue arrives. That would be the most us ending possible and I refuse.

Three hours. We did it. We actually did it.

*sits down for just a second because legs have gone a bit wobbly*

Okay. Okay I'm good. Let's clean up.

day_5.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
day_5.response:
Yeah? What was it like?

I dreamed about my bed. Like that was literally the whole dream, just my bed, my pillow, the exact weight of my own blanket. Nothing even happened in it. But I woke up and for about half a second I thought I was actually there and then...nope. Still here. Ground still hard.

But three hours Michelangelo. Three hours and you get to actually go home to the real version of whatever you dreamed about. That's not nothing. That's everything.

What did you dream about?

How much is there?

Look, I'm not going to blow up at you right now. We're three hours from rescue and I don't have the energy for it and honestly...it doesn't matter the same way it would have four days ago.

But I want you to understand something. There were moments out here - real moments - where Michelangelo was falling apart and DaVinci was losing it and I was running on fumes trying to hold things together, and this whole time you had a stash sitting somewhere. That's the bit that stings. Not the food itself. The fact that the rest of us didn't know it was there when we needed something to hold onto.

You said "for emergencies." What were you waiting for? Because from where I was standing we had a few of those.

*looks at the food for a second*

Eat it. Or share it, whatever you want to do with it. But when we get home and we're sitting somewhere safe and warm and this is all just a story we tell people - I want you to actually think about why you kept it separate. Not because I'm angry. Because I think you're smarter than that decision and I think somewhere you know it too.

You're a good person Donatello. You're just really bad at letting people in when it counts.

day_5.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
day_5.response:
*reads the last page*

Honestly? I'd be less scared of saying the hard thing in the moment. Like there were a few times where I noticed something was off - with you, with DaVinci, with the supplies - and I kind of circled around it for a bit before actually just...saying it. Trying to be diplomatic when sometimes you just need to be direct.

And I'd check on Michelangelo more. Like I tried, but I think there were moments where I got caught up in the logistics of keeping us alive and forgot that keeping someone mentally in one piece is just as important. He was struggling more than I probably fully registered at the time.

What would I keep? The rule about everyone getting a vote. I'd keep that. And the thing where we said no more information held back from the group. That one actually changed things when we enforced it.

*hands the notebook back*

What's your answer? You wrote the question, you must have some idea.

And for what it's worth - this notebook is going to matter to someone. Like if this ever happens to someone else and they find this written up somewhere, this is genuinely useful. You documented something real. That's not nothing.

Add that to your list of things you left behind, since apparently we're all worried about that lately.

day_5.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
day_5.response:
Ha, of course you are. That is so completely and utterly you and I mean that in the best possible way.

Honestly though? Do it. Like actually do it. Because that data is real and it's accurate and if anyone ever has to survive something like this again - whether it's researchers or rescue teams or just some poor person trying to figure out what to do - that report could genuinely matter.

Put me in the acknowledgements.

*laughs, a bit wobbly, still running on adrenaline and not much else*

No but seriously. You kept meticulous records under genuinely insane conditions and you never stopped thinking even when the rest of us were falling apart. That's remarkable Donatello, even if you drove me absolutely up the wall doing it.

Just...maybe in the report, include the people stuff too. Not just the resource data. Because the resource data tells you how much water four people need to survive five days. But the other stuff - the trust, the communication, the moments where it almost went sideways - that's what actually kept us alive. And that's harder to quantify but it's just as important.

You've got three hours. Start drafting it if you need something to do with your hands. I'll answer questions if you need to fill in any gaps from my end.

day_5.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
day_5.response:
None. They served no practical purpose at all.

*still not moving, watching the boat get bigger on the horizon*

But that's kind of the whole point isn't it. We were out here fighting to survive and DaVinci drew flowers next to an SOS sign because he's DaVinci and that's who he is, and...I don't know. It made me laugh. It made this place feel slightly less like somewhere we were going to die in.

I think that's what it was for. Not survival. Just...humanity. Proof that we were still ourselves even out here.

*voice goes a bit quiet*

I couldn't move when I saw the boat. Did you notice that? Everyone else reacted and I just...stood there. I don't know what that is. Relief I think, but it's too big to actually feel properly yet. Like my brain knows it's over but the rest of me hasn't caught up.

Donatello why are you sitting on the ground.

*looks at her, then back at the boat, then sits down next to her*

Okay yeah. Actually. Yeah. Let's just sit here for a second and watch it come in. We've earned that.

day_5.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
day_5.response:
Yeah. I know what you mean.

It's weird isn't it. You spend every single minute out here wanting to leave and then the boat actually shows up and something in you just...hesitates. Like leaving makes it real in a different way. Like we have to go back and be normal people who have jobs and sleep in beds and explain this to people who weren't here and will never quite understand it no matter how many times we try.

*looks at DaVinci standing there waiting*

He's so good. He's genuinely so good. Look at him, he stopped cheering just to check if we were okay. That's DaVinci.

I think I'm not ready either. And I also think we don't actually have a choice because that boat is coming whether we're ready or not, so.

*stands up slowly, reaches a hand down to Donatello*

Come on. Up you get. We did five days out here, we can do the next five minutes.

And then we go home.

day_5.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
day_5.response:
Yeah. I'm going.

*starts walking toward the water*

Come on Michelangelo, stay close. And yes DaVinci - we're going to be okay. I genuinely believe that. It's not going to be easy and I think we're all going to have some stuff to work through when we get back, that would be insane not to. But we're okay. We made it.

All four of us.

Now let's go before I start crying and I absolutely cannot be crying when we get on that boat, I have a reputation to maintain.
